I puts them in the pan.
The sentence needs “put” with “I”: “I put them in the pan.” Please try that sentence again.
Why not puts?
In the present tense, “puts” goes with “he,” “she,” or “it”; “I” takes “put.” The same retry is waiting whenever you’re ready, or you can skip it.
